title: Facebook Live for Business: How to Sell Products Live
summary: Learn how to set up Facebook Live for business, use Facebook Shop, stream product demos, answer questions, and turn live viewers into customers.
body_markdown:
Facebook Live lets you stream live video to the people who follow your Facebook Page. Instead of posting a photo or a video about your business and waiting for the reactions and comments to flow in, you turn on a camera and speak about your products while people watch and ask questions. For an ecommerce business, it’s a way to get prospective customers acquainted with the products and people behind your brand.


Shoppers are already buying through live video: US livestream ecommerce sales grew almost 50% to an estimated $14.64 billion in 2025, according to[eMarketer’s forecast](https://www.emarketer.com/content/faq-on-livestream-commerce--what-marketers-need-know-about-live-shopping-2026) . If Facebook is already part of your[marketing strategy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/marketing-strategy) , Facebook Live lets you take advantage of a platform you’re already on. You don’t need a separate tool to manage the stream, and your followers don’t need to download a different app to tune in.


Here’s what Facebook Live for business is, how to go live, and how to use it as part of your[social selling](https://www.shopify.com/blog/social-selling) strategy.


## What is Facebook Live for business?


[Facebook Live](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/216491699144904?id=1123223941353904) is Meta’s live video tool. For a business, it’s a way to share new or upcoming products, debut promotions, and give viewers a behind-the-scenes look at your business.


Livestreaming on Facebook lets you interact with customers, answer questions in real time, and get feedback. And if you’ve set up the[Facebook and Instagram by Meta sales channel](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/social-commerce/facebook-instagram-by-meta) , you can sync your Shopify catalog to Facebook, so you can sell the products you’re discussing. You pin products to the live video, which directs viewers to your online store where they can complete the purchase.


Start selling your products on Facebook


Shopify comes with powerful tools that help you list, promote and sell products on Facebook. Create product collections, showcase your brand and products, and make sales on Facebook from one place.


[Start selling on Facebook](https://www.shopify.com/facebook-instagram?itcat=coreblog&itterm=shopify-facebook-instagram-sales-channel-cta)


## How to sell products live on Facebook


1. Sync your product catalog and set up a Facebook Shop
2. Go live
3. Show the products and answer questions in real time
4. Use pinned comments and polls to manage the chat


Follow this step-by-step guide to prepare your Facebook account for live selling:


### 1. Sync your product catalog and set up a Facebook Shop


Meta has a few[requirement](https://www.facebook.com/help/1636872026560015) s for a business to go live: your account must be at least 60 days old, and your Page or professional mode profile must have at least 100 followers. If someone other than the Page owner hosts the stream, a Page admin needs to first permit them to post on the Page.


You can also go live from your personal profile, as long as you’ve turned on professional mode and have 100 followers or more.


Before your first broadcast, connect the[Facebook and Instagram by Meta sales channel](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/social-commerce/facebook-instagram-by-meta/index) in your Shopify admin. You’ll also need a verified business page, so you can create a Shop section and add a Shop Now button.


Once your channels are synced, you can add products to a catalog on Facebook and Instagram, and that catalog powers your[Facebook Shop](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/social-commerce/facebook-instagram-by-meta/facebook-shop) and[Instagram Shopping](https://help.instagram.com/337910740093030) . When you make changes to your products in Shopify, those changes show up in your Facebook Shop, and you can manage orders and customer data from your Shopify admin.


Having your products on the Shop lets you pin them to your live feed so viewers can find what you showed on camera. Use the same product names on the stream that appear in your catalog, and pin the comment pointing viewers to your Shop.


### 2. Go live


Once you have access, there are a few ways to use Facebook Live:


#### From your phone


Going live from your phone using the Facebook mobile app is the quickest option:


1.


Open the Facebook app and go to your Feed or your Page.


2.


Tap the What’s on your mind? box, then tap Live video. Allow camera and microphone access if you’re prompted.


3.


Select your audience and add a description. Options for the audience include Public, Friends, Friends except, Specific friends, Only me, and Close friends. (These options apply when you go live from a profile; live videos from a Page are public by default.)


4.


Tap Go live. You’ll have the option to invite guests to join on video, raise money for nonprofits and fundraisers, and create a poll.


*Source: Facebook*


#### From a computer with a webcam


Going live from a computer gives you a few more controls than the phone app.


1.


Click Live video from your Feed or your Page, or go to Meta Business Suite home and click Go live.


2.


Choose between going live now or scheduling a live event for later, then click Set up live video.


3.


Select the audience you want to broadcast to above the Stream setup tab.


4.


Under Select a video source, choose Webcam. Then use the Camera controls section to check that your camera and microphone inputs are working, picking the right ones from the dropdowns. There’s also a Start screen share button if you want to broadcast your screen.


5.


Check how you look in the Video panel (click Expand video for a bigger preview), then add a title and description. If you’re streaming from a Page, you can also notify Messenger subscribers and share the live video to your story (cross-posting to other Pages you manage works too).


6.


Click Go live.


*Source: Facebook* *Source: Facebook*


#### With streaming software


Streaming software allows you to use more than one camera as well as show on-screen graphics, and some tools can also stream to multiple platforms at once. Two options for Facebook Live are[Open Broadcaster Software (OBS)](https://obsproject.com/) and[Streamlabs](https://streamlabs.com/pt-pt/?srsltid=AU7gw4W3t63-9nMFCpjKHH8p4XQaiMmXpDHmwRlfbW9hdw7wwvEyPNTp) . OBS is free and open source. To use OBS:


1.


Add your camera as a video source.


2.


Click Settings. Under Stream, select Facebook Live as your service.


3.


Click Get stream key, which opens Live Producer.


4.


In Live Producer, choose Streaming software under Select a video source, then copy your stream key (an alphanumeric password).


5.


Paste the stream key into OBS and start your stream. The Video panel in Live Producer says “Connect streaming software to go live” until your feed comes through, then shows a preview. Once you start previewing the broadcast, you have up to four hours to go live.


6.


Click Go live.


*Source: Facebook*


### 3. Show the product and answer questions in real time


Going live allows you to answer viewers’ questions on the spot. April Mall, cofounder of the online plant nursery[Unsolicited Plant Talks](https://unsolicitedplanttalks.com/) , has embraced live selling and says her community of greenery enthusiasts loves it.


“It’s one thing to see me on a Reel or a story or a static post photo. And it’s another thing to actually show them the plants, talk about the care, talk about pros and cons of that plant,” April says on an episode of[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/unsolicited-plant-talks-hobby-to-business) . “They can make a better decision if that plant is specifically for them. And they can ask me questions in real time. ‘If I buy this plant, will this south-facing window work for it? Does it need lots of humidity?’ And I can give them care right there and then.”


To get the most out of your own broadcasts, think about the questions you already get by email and in customer reviews. Hold up your products to demonstrate scale and whatever functionality matters—put it on, open it, pour it, or plug it in. If you don’t know the answer to a question someone asks, say so and follow up in the comments or with a dedicated Facebook post afterward.


After the stream ends, viewers can also message you through Facebook Messenger or the Contact Seller button.


### 4. Use pinned comments and polls to manage the chat


A busy chat moves quickly. The message you most want viewers to see, like pinned products,[discount codes](https://www.shopify.com/blog/discounts-and-coupons) , or a reminder to check the Shop section, can scroll out of view in seconds. To solve this, pin crucial information to the top of the chat so it’s easy to find. You can only pin one comment at a time, but you can change it as often as you like, which is useful if you’re showing different products and want to pin the one you’re currently talking about.


You can also set up polls ahead of time and launch them during your live video. When you’re live, launch the poll from the Interactivity menu on a computer or the Features menu in the app. Polls give viewers something to do and tell you what they want. For instance, if you’re a sneaker brand, you could have them vote on which colorway to restock or which product you should bring to market next.

## Tips for using Facebook Live to drive sales


- Stream on a schedule
- Get more out of the replay
- Treat Facebook Live as part of a broader strategy


Here are some tips for using livestreaming on Facebook as part of your overall marketing strategy to build engagement and boost sales:


### Stream on a schedule


Making your stream a recurring series gives customers a reason to come back. If you run an online store, consider a weekly or monthly stream built around something like new stock as it arrives or a product of the week. Having a set time that viewers know you’ll appear makes it easier for them to make watching a regular habit.


[Revenge Of](https://revengeof.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4WfCViJsVzkokL6XhntKMQ89zDAq5Bw5F_3abgC2mh2kjPFCLLF) , a comic shop and pinball arcade in Los Angeles, built their weekly broadcast around the day new comics arrive. Cofounder Joe Myers says on an[episode of Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/revenge-of-community-growth-strategies-that-drive-sales) : “We run down some of our favorites in a livestream in which we’re interacting directly with customers who are both e-com as well as in-store. And we’re getting comments and interactions that way.” He adds that the stream has become an entry point for newcomers and a way to keep regular customers engaged.


You can schedule streams up to 24 hours ahead using the Later option in Live Producer. Scheduling doesn’t notify your followers, though. To let them know in advance,[create a Live video event](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2087325741287572?id=1123223941353904) instead.


### Get more out of the replay


Once you press End Live Video, the video stays on your Facebook Page for 30 days, after which Meta automatically removes it. During the 30-day window, you can share the replay or download it to use on your website. You can also clip short moments from your Facebook Live videos to repurpose for social media and your website.


For example, you could pull a 40-second clip of you answering a question and embed it on a[product page](https://www.shopify.com/blog/product-page) , or create Reels out of key moments.


### Treat Facebook Live as part of a broader strategy


Your livestream is one piece of how you[build your brand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-build-a-brand) online. Jess from Revenge Of describes the effort to bring the store’s brand online: “We’ve done an immense amount of work to carry that brand over into the digital space through Instagram and Facebook and the ecommerce site.” He adds that livestreams are also a place to pitch specific products, which gets customers excited about talking about those products with other people.


Cross-promotion is one way to connect your livestream to the rest of your marketing. Let your followers on Instagram and your email list know when you’ll be broadcasting next, and add the replay to your website if that’s where most of your customers are. You can also run more than one social commerce channel, like pairing Facebook Live with[TikTok Live](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-go-live-on-tiktok) and[TikTok Shop](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tiktok-shop-features) , if your customers are spread across platforms.


## Facebook Live for business FAQ


### Can a business page go live on Facebook?


Yes, as long as your Facebook account is at least 60 days old and the Facebook Page you’re broadcasting from has at least 100 followers.


### How do I create a Facebook Live stream?


You can go live on your Facebook Page from your phone or a computer. You can also use streaming software such as Open Broadcaster Software (OBS), which lets you use more than one camera and show on-screen graphics.


### How much does it cost to livestream on Facebook?


Livestreaming on Facebook from your phone or computer is free, as is Open Broadcaster Software (OBS) if you want to use dedicated streaming software. Additional equipment like a dedicated camera, lighting, or a microphone is an added cost, but it can improve your livestream quality.
